title: One app, two processes
desc: A drawing of an app file on disk, the process created to run it, the saved screen description kept outside that process, and a second process created later with a new number and empty memory.

steps.note: Your app is a file on disk. None of your code is running yet.
Android needs to run it, so the kernel creates a process and gives it a number.
Everything your code makes lives in that process: objects, singletons, threads.
Before your app goes to the background, the system writes down a small description of the screen, outside your process.
Memory runs short while the user is elsewhere. The process ends, and none of your code runs.
The user comes back. New process, new number, empty memory, screen rebuilt from the description.
